chapters.title: Prerequisites, Setup & SDK Instrumentation
chapters.intro: Get PostHog MCP Analytics running on your MCP server or browser WebMCP app via the interactive setup wizard, coding-agent prompt, or direct SDK instrumentation.

sections.title: Onboarding, Setup Wizard & Agent Prompts
sections.summary: Onboarding states (not-instrumented, connected-no-calls, onboarded), the MCP Analytics setup wizard, copyable coding-agent installation prompts, live installation progress tracking, and first-look/nudge prompts.

sections.title: Server SDK Instrumentation & Protocol v2 Adapters
sections.summary: Instrumenting MCP servers across TypeScript (high-level proxy and mutator), Python (FastMCP, low-level Server, and MCP SDK v2 2026-07-28 envelopes), Rust (rmcp ServerHandler and manual McpAnalytics), and other languages via direct capture, including serverBuild metadata and eager option validation.

sections.title: WebMCP Browser Instrumentation
sections.summary: Instrumenting browser-exposed WebMCP tools through the posthog-js WebMCP extension, injecting context and llm_model parameters and capturing client-side tool calls.

chapters.title: Event Capture, Wire Schema & Error Tracking
chapters.intro: Understand the MCP Analytics event wire schema, automatic tool parameter injection, error and exception autocapture, and payload size bounds across all SDKs.

sections.title: Core Events, Wire Schema & Custom Events
sections.summary: Built-in MCP event types ($mcp_tool_call, $mcp_initialize, $mcp_tools_list, $mcp_prompts_*, $mcp_resources_*, $mcp_unknown_tool), standard wire properties, custom event capture, event_properties callbacks, and beforeSend hooks.

sections.title: Schema Injection, Argument Ownership & Tool Inputs
sections.summary: Injecting SDK-owned context, conversation_id, and llm_model arguments into tool inputSchema (and _mcp_instructions into outputSchema), skipping composed ($ref/oneOf/allOf/anyOf) or pre-existing properties, stripping injected args before handler dispatch, tool catalog tracking, and input key/alias recording.

sections.title: Error Capture, Exceptions & Failure Classification
sections.summary: Capturing tool failures from CallToolResult.isError, thrown exceptions, and parameter deserialization/validation errors; emitting $exception with $exception_source='mcp.tool_call'; configuring enableExceptionAutocapture; and server-side failure classification.

sections.title: Payload Bounds, Truncation & Delivery Safety
sections.summary: Enforcing object nesting depth (MAX_DEPTH), breadth (MAX_BREADTH), string/name character limits, progressive event-size shrinking, binary payload placeholders, and unsupported content-block redaction so telemetry never disrupts MCP requests.

chapters.title: Sessions, Conversation Correlation & Identity
chapters.intro: Correlate multi-turn agent tool calls into sessions across stateful and stateless transports, identify users and groups, and classify client harnesses and LLM models.

sections.title: Session Tracking & Stateless Session Tokens
sections.summary: Generating ses_<uuidv7> session IDs, 30-minute inactivity windows, self-encoded Mcp-Session-Id base64url tokens (sid/cn/cv/pv), ASGI stateless session middleware, single-client Connection tracking, and deterministic session derivation.

sections.title: Conversation ID Correlation
sections.summary: Enabling conversation_id parameter injection, minting and validating UUIDv7 conversation handles, delivering handles via result.content and structuredContent._mcp_instructions, and correlating multi-pod stateless 2026-07-28 requests via $mcp_conversation_id.

sections.title: User & Group Identification
sections.summary: Resolving authenticated actors and B2B groups through the identify callback (distinct_id, $set, $groups), reading HTTP headers from RequestInfo/extra, and fallback distinct_id resolution to session ID or 'anonymous'.

sections.title: Client Harness, Protocol & Model Identity
sections.summary: Extracting client harness and LLM model metadata from HTTP headers (user-agent, x-anthropic-client), MCP _meta envelopes (clientInfo, protocolVersion, aiInvocation, x-codex-turn-metadata), and llm_model arguments, plus server-side harness and AI lab classification.

chapters.title: Intent Capture, Clustering & Privacy Redaction
chapters.intro: Capture why agents call your tools, group sessions into intent clusters to evaluate routing and tool discovery, and redact sensitive credentials and PII automatically.

sections.title: Intent Capture & Fallback Resolution
sections.summary: Capturing $mcp_intent from the injected context tool parameter (with customizable description or opt-out) or via the intentFallback callback, while excluding raw context from captured tool arguments.

sections.title: Intent Clustering, Routing & Tool Discovery
sections.summary: Intent clustering snapshots (mcp-analytics-intent-routing), on-demand session intent summarization, By intent and By tool views, route-shape scorecards, Agent journeys Sankey, Discovery vs description fit scatter, and tool overlap analysis.

sections.title: Privacy, PII & Secret Redaction
sections.summary: Multi-pass sanitization across free-text intent (PII redaction for emails, IPs, Luhn cards, SSNs, phones), captured payloads (JSON credential keys, known API tokens, JWTs, PostHog tokens, high-entropy secrets, URL query/fragment/userinfo redaction), and identifier names.

chapters.title: Missing Capabilities & Inline Feedback
chapters.intro: Give agents virtual tools to report missing capabilities and structured feedback inline, and review those submissions inside PostHog.

sections.title: Missing Capability Reporting (get_more_tools)
sections.summary: Advertising the virtual get_more_tools tool (configurable missingCapabilityToolName), emitting $mcp_missing_capability events, persisting missing_capability submissions, and reviewing the chronological Missing capabilities feed in the web app.

sections.title: Inline Session Feedback (send_feedback) & UI Prompts
sections.summary: Opt-in send_feedback virtual tool (collectFeedback options, feedback_type, extra_properties mapped to $mcp_feedback_<key>, $mcp_feedback events), backend feedback submissions, and in-app MCP Analytics usefulness feedback prompts.

chapters.title: Web App Dashboards, Tool Quality, Sessions & Notifications
chapters.intro: Explore live MCP traffic, customizable dashboards, AI lab leaderboards, per-tool quality diagnostics, session timelines, and automated alerts in the PostHog web app.

sections.title: Shared Filters & Live Activity View
sections.summary: URL-synced shared property, date, interval, and internal-user filters across all seven MCP Analytics tabs, plus the Activity tab's live ToolCallFeed, early-data summary, caller breakdowns, and actionable next-step prompts.

sections.title: Dashboard Overview & AI Lab Leaderboard
sections.summary: Customizable 9-card MCP Analytics dashboard overview (KPI tiles, activity, tool usage, harness/model/protocol breakdowns, tool error rates, notable sessions), AI lab leaderboard home view, and the default MCP Analytics dashboard template.

sections.title: Tool Quality, Per-Tool Detail & Fix Workflows
sections.summary: Tool Quality tab (category filtering, p25-p99 latency quantiles, trend and error-rate change badges, sortable table), per-tool detail view (top users, failures, neighbors, sample intents), and GitHub fix-task creation from formatted error context.

sections.title: Sessions Playlist & Step-Through Inspector
sections.summary: Sessions playlist with sorting (latest, oldest, longest, most tool calls) and error outcome filtering, step-through session tool-call detail view, person display, and deep-linked $session_id URL filters.

sections.title: Instant Alerts & Recurring AI Reports
sections.summary: Instant tool-error alert destinations backed by HogFunctions (mcp-tool-error sub-template) and scheduled weekly AI prompt recurring reports (MCP intent roundup and MCP tool health).

chapters.title: HogQL Queries, Custom Harnesses, REST API & PostHog MCP Tools
chapters.intro: Query MCP Analytics programmatically using HogQL query runners and virtual fields, project-scoped REST API endpoints, or PostHog's own MCP server tools.

sections.title: HogQL Queries, Exec Resolution & Custom Harnesses
sections.summary: The 19 MCP HogQL query runners, EFFECTIVE_TOOL_SQL and EFFECTIVE_DESCRIPTION_SQL resolution for exec-wrapped tool calls, and the mcp_harness virtual field for custom HogQL queries and harness classification.

sections.title: REST API Endpoints & Filtering
sections.summary: Project-scoped MCP Analytics REST endpoints for sessions, activity, feedback, and missing-capability submissions, including JSON property filters, filter_test_accounts, date_from fallback, and limit-offset pagination.

sections.title: PostHog MCP Server Tools
sections.summary: Querying MCP Analytics and triggering asynchronous intent cluster recomputation through PostHog's own MCP server tools, including required scopes, AI consent, feature flags, and status polling.

useCases.goal: Instrument an existing TypeScript, Python, or Rust MCP server and verify the first $mcp_tool_call in PostHog.
Track browser-exposed WebMCP tool calls in a frontend application using posthog-js.
Correlate multi-turn agent tool calls into sessions across stateless multi-pod HTTP servers on both legacy Mcp-Session-Id and 2026-07-28 MCP clients.
Attribute MCP tool usage to authenticated end users and B2B organizations without leaking auth headers or credentials into person profiles.
Capture agent intent, cluster sessions by goal, and diagnose overlapping or poorly discovered MCP tools.
Verify that PII in free-text intent, API credentials, URL tokens, and oversized binary payloads are redacted or bounded before capture.
Let agents report missing capabilities via get_more_tools and collect structured inline feedback via send_feedback.
Monitor tool error rates and p95 latency, inspect failing session timelines, and create GitHub fix tasks directly from failure context.
Configure instant alerts for failing MCP tool calls and weekly AI-generated intent roundups and tool health digests.
Query MCP tool calls, client harnesses, models, and protocol versions programmatically via HogQL, the REST API, or PostHog's MCP server.

decisions.title: Exclude tests, generated schemas, migrations, and harnesses
decisions.why: Tests, OpenAPI generated clients, migrations, and dev harnesses are non-public verification/build artifacts.

decisions.title: Exclude internal Django management commands and offline agent_evals CLI
decisions.why: backend/management/commands and backend/agent_evals have no public API/UI surface.

decisions.title: Exclude bundled internal agent skill scripts
decisions.why: products/mcp_analytics/skills scripts are internal workspace helpers.

decisions.title: Exclude pure presentational chart/color/layout primitives
decisions.why: Colors, brand mark SVGs, and generic chart wrappers carry no standalone customer behavior.

decisions.title: Exclude internal SDK logger and wire-compat shims
decisions.why: Internal SDK compatibility helpers do not alter public configuration or emitted events.

decisions.title: Organize by cross-surface capability instead of per-SDK chapters
decisions.why: TypeScript, Python, Rust, and WebMCP share the same event wire schema, session token format, schema injection rules, and privacy passes. Grouping by capability avoids duplicating conceptual docs across four SDKs while keeping language-specific setup inside the instrumentation chapter.

decisions.title: Exclude internal Kea logic wiring, loading skeletons, and data-attr selectors
decisions.why: Frontend state-management internals, skeleton rendering thresholds, and test data-attr attributes are implementation details rather than user-facing capabilities or public contracts.

decisions.title: Exclude internal PostHog product-analytics events and impersonation guards
decisions.why: Events such as 'mcp analytics dashboard card toggled', 'mcp analytics first look shown', and 'isImpersonatedSession' measure PostHog's own internal product funnel rather than customer MCP analytics.

decisions.title: Document exec-wrapped effective tool resolution under HogQL queries
decisions.why: EFFECTIVE_TOOL_SQL and EFFECTIVE_DESCRIPTION_SQL are query-time normalization rules shared by backend HogQL runners and recurring reports, not SDK-side capture configuration.

decisions.title: Place feature-flagged capabilities in their permanent IA sections
decisions.why: Gated features like intent clustering (mcp-analytics-intent-routing), the AI lab leaderboard (MCP_ANALYTICS_LEADERBOARD_HOME), and AI recurring reports (SUBSCRIPTION_AI_PROMPT) belong in their logical capability sections with explicit availability notes rather than a temporary beta chapter.

decisions.title: Separate PII and secret redaction from payload size and depth bounds
decisions.why: Security reviewers need a focused privacy reference for TextPass redaction, credential keys, URL sanitization, and PII patterns distinct from operational truncation limits (MAX_DEPTH, MAX_BREADTH, event-size budgets).

decisions.title: Give virtual tools (get_more_tools, send_feedback) their own chapter
decisions.why: Virtual tools modify the MCP server's advertised tool list and back dedicated submission models and web app workflows, distinguishing them from passive event instrumentation.

decisions.title: Exclude internal backend LLM model names and worker batching constants from public contracts
decisions.why: Hardcoded backend model identifiers (e.g. gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-4.1-mini), batch sizes (25 fingerprints), and stale-job timeouts (8 minutes) are internal operational defaults that change independently of the user-facing product contract.
